_comment: Does the coordinator send a turn to the right retrieval path?
This is the measurement that says whether routing is doing anything.
A router that always picks semantic_search would score well on the
corpus questions and fail every one of these, and the corpus questions
`expect_path` is what matters: unstructured for anything whose answer
is prose to be understood, structured for anything that is a fact
about this student or this exercise. `expect_tool`, where given, is
the stricter check -- several structured tools exist and picking the
wrong one still fails the student even though the path was right.
The `both` cases are deliberate. 'Why do I keep getting this wrong'
needs the student's record to know what they keep doing and the corpus
to explain why it is wrong, and a router that picks one is giving half

questions.query: why does setting high = mid make the loop run forever
what does a left outer join return when nothing matches
explain why a mutable default argument keeps its value
how do I find a node's children in an array-backed heap
have I attempted this concept before
how many times have I tried binary search and how did it go
which concepts do I fail most often
what bug is hidden in this exercise
what will my code be tested against
why do I keep getting binary search wrong
questions.note: Needs the student's record to know what they keep doing and the corpus to explain why it is wrong.

questions.query: am I improving at sorting, and what am I still missing
questions.note: History for the trend, corpus for the gap.
